| [CLAIM-682](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-682.md) v4 | A dependence becomes presumptively dominating by those who control it when three conditions coincide: participation in an important sphere of life rests on the arrangement, those who control it hold consequential discretion over the dependent, and the dependent lacks effective means of protection, influence, challenge or justified withdrawal; this is a test for domination by an arrangement's controllers, not for every unfreedom, and impersonal constraint that no one holds is outside it | A's, from A13 §II of the exchange "Analyze technological civilization trap" (2026-11-13): a dependence is presumptively dominating by those who control it when essentiality, asymmetrical authority and inadequate accountability coincide. The claim is now a test for domination by an arrangement's controllers, not for every unfreedom. Zuboff 2022 is a worked case of all three conditions ([THEORY-1842](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1842.md)). Interpretive. The wording is A's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-684](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-684.md) v2 | When a choice about a technology or an institution could substantially and durably narrow the possibilities later open to those it affects, the burden of justifying it should rise with the size and the irreversibility of the narrowing | A's, A13 §VIII of the exchange "Analyze technological civilization trap" (2026-11-13), "the reversibility principle", offered as "a practical formulation of restraint": "When a technological choice could substantially and durably narrow future human possibilities, the burden of justification should rise with the magnitude and irreversibility of the change." It answers the ratchet A described ([CLAIM-677](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-677.md)) with a rule for deciding before lock-in, and A pairs it with pilots, independent evaluation and appeals. The record holds that provisional activation and later cancellation can both be optimal under informative reassessment ([CLAIM-559](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-559.md)), which is one reason irreversibility matters, and that anchors entrench ([CLAIM-184](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-184.md)); it holds no principle for the burden of justification. Interpretive. The wording is A's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-686](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-686.md) v2 | Where a dependent party's claims on an arrangement's controllers fail of legibility, volitional efficacy or correctability in the controlling organization, the dependent lacks effective means of influence and challenge, and where they fail so at every party able to constrain the controllers it lacks effective protection; justified withdrawal lies outside those three achievements, so the domination threshold's third condition is met by failures of normative efficacy only together with a failure of exit, and is not those failures restated | The assistant's, from the step-12 ideas of the filing of the exchange "Analyze technological civilization trap" (2026-11-13), offered as "the threshold in the record's own terms" and accepted by the owner on 2026-11-13 ("file the still unfiled stuff"). The idea was that [CLAIM-682](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-682.md)'s third condition, inadequate accountability, could be restated as the failure of [CLAIM-523](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-523.md)'s legibility, volitional efficacy or correctability for the dependent party's claims, and that this held nearly by definition. Checked against both entries, it holds only in part. [CLAIM-523](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-523.md) states the three as needed, not as sufficient, so a failure of any one, for the dependent's claims, entails that the dependent lacks effective influence and challenge; the converse does not follow. Protection is the same failure at a third party able to constrain the controllers. Justified withdrawal is exit, which none of the three covers. So the restatement is narrower than the condition, and on the natural reading, that the dependent lacks all four kinds of means, the condition also needs exit to fail. Demonstrated; the derivation is in the body. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-687](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-687.md) v2 | The accountability that those who control an arrangement owe to those who depend on it should rise with how indispensable the arrangement has become to them, so that an arrangement that has become effectively compulsory owes public justification of its purposes and governing rules, and those affected owe no deference to expertise or ownership as such | A's, from the exchange "Analyze technological civilization trap" (2026-11-13), its "technological constitutionalism" (A8 §VII, A11 §24–25, A13 §VI.3–4): "The more indispensable a system becomes, the stronger its obligations of accountability should ordinarily be", with "Public justification" owed "When a technological arrangement becomes effectively compulsory". A's protections (refusal, contestability, portability, interoperability, human competence, accountability, resilience) and its formula "Specialized competence in operation, public accountability in purpose, and enforceable rights for those affected" are how it would be met. Interpretive. Filed on 2026-11-13 from the items the first filing left. The wording is A's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-689](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-689.md) | Whether a desire was formed by social influence and whether its object is worth desiring are separate questions; since every preference is socially formed, a critique of produced wants cannot rest on their origin alone, and can ask instead whether satisfying them engages people with anything worthwhile | A's, A9 §III of the exchange "Analyze technological civilization trap" (2026-11-13), after the owner's U7: "We should distinguish how a desire originated from whether its object is worth desiring", since "The fact that a preference has been shaped by society cannot, on its own, establish that it is undesirable." | [CLAIM-690](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-690.md) v2 | Whichever way a whole and its part depend on each other, the same magnitude of dependence can run either way, and what sorts it is who controls the terms on which it is met, exit, renegotiation and the conditions of supply, while the magnitude and the integration that produced it set only how much rides on it: with the part able to withdraw or renegotiate, the whole's need of it becomes the part's hold on its terms; with the terms at an agent's discretion, the same need gives the part none, and the part's own dependence becomes vulnerability to that agent, on whom, under a principle grounding obligations in such vulnerability, the strengthened responsibility falls | The assistant's, offered at step 12 of the filing of "About Plantation Paradise" ([#488](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/488)) and accepted by the owner on 2026-11-13. The record asks the whole-part dependence question in two directions: when a whole's dependence on a part becomes the part's authority ([QUESTION-461](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-461.md)), and when a part's dependence on a whole strengthens someone's obligations to it ([CLAIM-671](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-671.md), [QUESTION-460](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-460.md)). In both, the record's answer turns on the same variable: who controls the terms on which the dependence is met, not how great it is, and not how deep the integration that produced it ([CLAIM-603](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-603.md)'s route). Grounded in a fictional case of equal dependence and different control over exit ([CASE-264](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-264.md)); the inference is [ARG-110](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-110.md). It keeps the ground of an obligation apart from its bearer, as the owner's review of [#488](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/488) asked: control fixes on whom a strengthened responsibility falls, not whether the principle that grounds it holds. Interpretive. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
